key_insight: LLM agents can reliably turn natural-language household preferences into near-optimal home energy schedules when they can call tools directly.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical interface layer for home energy management systems that can automate flexible appliance scheduling, reduce costs, and support demand-response participation.
method: Built a ReAct-style tool-calling agent for multi-appliance scheduling
Integrated live Agile electricity prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against a MILP ground truth
evidence_signal: Across tariff, conflict, solar-cooptimization, and week-long tests, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and agents captured 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Reliability drops sharply with text-parsed action interfaces, and real-world deployment still depends on robust handling of infeasible constraints and changing household conditions.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
